newsitem.title: THAILAND: Electric Generating eases in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Electric Generating eases in early trade.

text.p: Private power producer Electricity Generating Plc (EGCO) retreated during early Monday trade on weak market sentiment and a poor outlook for the economy, analysts said on Monday.
EGCO was down 1.50 baht to 55 baht as of 0442 GMT.
"Investors are selling because of poor sentiment and EGCO is caught in the bearish mood although it's considered a good stock in the energy sector," said an analyst.
Analysts said, however, that investors should buy EGCO for medium and long-term investment.

"Investors ought to accumulate EGCO for either medium or long term as the stock would hardly be affected by the country's economy slowdown," said Busaba Kunasirin, of Chao Phya Finance and Securities.
Busaba said EGCO would benefit from steadily rising electricity demand in Thailand.
Electricity Generating currently has two plants -- a 1,200-megawatt generator in eastern Rayong province and a 824-megawatt plant in southern Nakhon Si Thammarat province.
